assumptions: Success rate means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Early September is assumed to mean 1-10 September 2026, compared against the prior 10 days (22-31 August 2026).
The metric is attempt_success_rate for UPI.
caveats: The data-quality scan found no issues, so no data-quality caveats apply.
The hour-of-day view for Zephyr was shown only for hours 0-11 in the evidence rows; the significant evening hours are taken from the summary of significant hours.

facts.text: UPI attempt success rate was 92.1% in 1-10 Sep (58,146 successes out of 63,131 attempts), compared with 93.0% in 22-31 Aug (60,069 out of 64,606 attempts). That is a fall of 0.87pp.
The change is statistically significant (p-value 2.78e-09) and the confidence intervals do not overlap: 92.78%-93.17% in the baseline versus 91.89%-92.31% in the current window.
Attempt volume was similar across the two windows: 64,606 baseline attempts versus 63,131 current attempts.
In the daily series, the rate was 92.6% on 1 Sep and 91.8% on 2 Sep, against a late-August range of roughly 92.2% to 93.4%. No anomaly windows were flagged in the daily series.
Issuer is the dimension that best concentrates the change. Zephyr's UPI success rate fell from 93.4% to 89.6%.
Within Zephyr, the hours with a statistically significant drop are 19, 20, 21 and 22. The worst is hour 19, which fell 11.92pp. Other hours shown (0-11) did not show a significant change.
For Zephyr, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts (53 to 745 failures), a rise of 3.61 per 100 attempts. This is the largest shift among Zephyr's failure codes.
Across all UPI, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT rose from 0.29 to 1.39 per 100 attempts (189 to 879 failures). Other failure codes moved by 0.15 per 100 attempts or less.
The data-quality scan found no issues for 1-10 Sep.

response.headline: UPI success rate fell 0.87pp, from 93.0% to 92.1%, in 1-10 September versus 22-31 August. The drop is statistically significant and is concentrated in one issuer, Zephyr, where UPI PSP timeouts jumped.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check Zephyr/PSP incident logs and latency for 19:00-22:59 from 1 Sep. Compare timeout rates by PSP handle and see if the issue started on a specific date using the hour-by-date view.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is concentrated in Zephyr and in hours 19-22. The failure-code shift is dominated by UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT, a technical code, while customer drop-off and issuer decline codes barely moved.
hypotheses.text: A PSP-side or Zephyr-side connectivity or latency problem in the evening hours (about 19:00-22:59) caused the extra UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT failures and most of the overall UPI decline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Re-run the segment scan excluding Zephyr and see whether any residual decline remains.
hypotheses.rationale: Other dimensions (acquirer, region, category, channel) showed much weaker concentration, so the evidence does not point to a second clear driver.
hypotheses.text: Part of the remaining overall decline may come from smaller drifts in other segments, since Zephyr's own fall (93.4% to 89.6%) is larger than the 0.87pp overall move.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A PSP-side or Zephyr-side connectivity or latency problem in the evening hours (about 19:00-22:59) caused the extra UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT failures and most of the overall UPI decline.
recommendations.rationale: Timeouts rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts for Zephyr and the significant drops are all in evening hours.
recommendations.text: Raise the Zephyr UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT spike with the PSP/issuer technical contact and ask for logs for the evening hours (19:00-22:59) from 1 Sep onward.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: For Zephyr, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts (53 to 745 failures), a rise of 3.61 per 100 attempts. This is the largest shift among Zephyr's failure codes.
recommendations.rationale: The overall UPI rate moved only 0.87pp, which was easy to miss, while the Zephyr evening hours dropped sharply.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts, split by issuer and hour of day.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Within Zephyr, the hours with a statistically significant drop are 19, 20, 21 and 22. The worst is hour 19, which fell 11.92pp. Other hours shown (0-11) did not show a significant change.
recommendations.rationale: The loss is concentrated in a specific issuer and time band, so a targeted mitigation could recover part of the 0.87pp drop.
recommendations.text: Consider routing or retry options for Zephyr UPI attempts during the affected evening hours while the timeouts are investigated.
